jehoiachin_791.name: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin_791.who: King of Judah who reigned three months before being taken captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.
key: He became king at eighteen and did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 24).
He surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and was exiled to Babylon with his family and officials (2 Kings 24).
Jeremiah declared that none of his offspring would sit on David's throne (Jeremiah 22).
In his thirty-seventh year of exile, Evil-merodach released him and gave him a place at his table (2 Kings 25).
He is listed as Jechoniah in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

jehoiada_792.name: Jehoiada
jehoiada_792.who: Father of Benaiah, the valiant man from Kabzeel who commanded David's bodyguard and later Solomon's army.
key: His son Benaiah was placed over David's Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Samuel 8).
A Jehoiada led 3,700 men of the house of Aaron to David at Hebron (1 Chronicles 12).
His son Benaiah is listed among David's mighty men for his heroic deeds (2 Samuel 23).
Benaiah helped make Solomon king and later replaced Joab as army commander (1 Kings 2).

joshua_893.name: Joshua
joshua_893.who: High priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and helped lead the rebuilding of the temple.
key: He returned from exile with Zerubbabel among the first group of exiles (Ezra 2).
He and Zerubbabel rebuilt the altar and laid the temple's foundation (Ezra 3).
Stirred by Haggai's preaching, he resumed work on the house of the LORD (Haggai 1).
In Zechariah's vision his filthy garments were replaced with clean ones (Zechariah 3).
Zechariah was told to set a crown on his head as a sign (Zechariah 6).

mary_1938.name: Mary
mary_1938.who: The virgin from Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph, who gave birth to Jesus the Messiah.
key: The angel Gabriel told her she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear Jesus (Luke 1).
She visited Elizabeth and praised God in a song of thanksgiving (Luke 1).
She gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem and laid him in a manger (Luke 2).
At the cross Jesus entrusted her to the care of the beloved disciple (John 19).
After the ascension she devoted herself to prayer with the disciples in Jerusalem (Acts 1).

abijah_38.name: Abijah
abijah_38.who: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam, who reigned three years in Jerusalem.
key: Rehoboam appointed him chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king (2 Chronicles 11).
He became king and walked in all the sins of his father (1 Kings 15).
From Mount Zemaraim he rebuked Jeroboam and Israel for forsaking the LORD (2 Chronicles 13).
Judah defeated Israel because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers (2 Chronicles 13).
He died, and his son Asa reigned in his place (2 Chronicles 14).

achish_66.name: Achish
achish_66.who: Philistine king of Gath who sheltered David while David was fleeing from Saul.
key: David pretended to be insane before him in order to escape (1 Samuel 21).
He later received David and his men and gave him the town of Ziklag (1 Samuel 27).
He planned to bring David with him to fight against Israel (1 Samuel 28).
When the Philistine commanders objected, he sent David back home (1 Samuel 29).
Shimei's runaway servants fled to him, and Shimei's pursuit led to his execution (1 Kings 2).

ahikam_141.name: Ahikam
ahikam_141.who: Royal official under King Josiah, son of Shaphan, who protected the prophet Jeremiah.
key: Josiah sent him with others to inquire of the prophetess Huldah about the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22).
He protected Jeremiah so that he was not handed over to be put to death (Jeremiah 26).
His son Gedaliah was appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25).
Jeremiah was entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam after Jerusalem fell (Jeremiah 39).

hilkiah_1524.name: Hilkiah
hilkiah_1524.who: High priest during King Josiah's reign who found the Book of the Law in the temple.
key: While the temple was being repaired, he found the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22).
He went with other officials to inquire of the prophetess Huldah (2 Kings 22).
At Josiah's command he removed the vessels made for Baal from the temple (2 Kings 23).
He gave thousands of animals to the priests for Josiah's Passover (2 Chronicles 35).
He is listed among the ancestors of Ezra the priest (Ezra 7).

ithamar_649.name: Ithamar
ithamar_649.who: Youngest son of Aaron, ordained as a priest and overseer of Levite duties at the tabernacle.
key: He was set apart with his father and brothers to serve as a priest (Exodus 28).
He directed the Levites' accounting of the materials used for the tabernacle (Exodus 38).
After Nadab and Abihu died, Moses told him and Eleazar not to mourn publicly (Leviticus 10).
He supervised the Gershonites and Merarites in carrying the tabernacle (Numbers 4).
His descendants formed eight of the priestly divisions in David's time (1 Chronicles 24).

jezebel_1605.name: Jezebel
jezebel_1605.who: Sidonian princess who married King Ahab of Israel and promoted Baal worship.
key: Ahab married her and began to serve and worship Baal (1 Kings 16).
She killed the prophets of the LORD and supported hundreds of Baal's prophets (1 Kings 18).
After Mount Carmel she vowed to kill Elijah, and he fled (1 Kings 19).
She arranged false charges against Naboth so Ahab could take his vineyard (1 Kings 21).
At Jehu's order she was thrown from a window, and dogs ate her body (2 Kings 9).

jotham_1735.name: Jotham
jotham_1735.who: King of Judah, son of Uzziah, who did what was right and grew strong.
key: He governed the people while his father Uzziah lived in isolation with leprosy (2 Kings 15).
He became king at twenty-five and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 27).
He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD (2 Kings 15).
He defeated the Ammonites, who paid him tribute for three years (2 Chronicles 27).
He grew mighty because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God (2 Chronicles 27).

naomi_2147.name: Naomi
naomi_2147.who: Woman of Bethlehem, mother-in-law of Ruth, who returned home from Moab after losing her family.
key: During a famine she moved to Moab, where her husband and both sons died (Ruth 1).
She returned to Bethlehem with Ruth and asked to be called Mara (Ruth 1).
She recognized Boaz as one of their redeemers (Ruth 2).
She instructed Ruth to go to Boaz at the threshing floor (Ruth 3).
She cared for Ruth's son Obed, and the women praised the LORD (Ruth 4).

cyrus_968.name: Cyrus
cyrus_968.who: King of Persia who allowed the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.
key: Isaiah named him as the LORD's shepherd who would order Jerusalem rebuilt (Isaiah 44).
The LORD called him his anointed, whose right hand he had grasped (Isaiah 45).
In his first year he decreed that the house of the LORD be rebuilt (Ezra 1).
He returned the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem (Ezra 1).
Daniel received a great vision in the third year of his reign (Daniel 10).

joash_1632.name: Joash
joash_1632.who: King of Judah, rescued as an infant, who repaired the temple but later turned from the LORD.
key: His aunt Jehosheba hid him in the temple for six years from Athaliah (2 Kings 11).
At age seven he was crowned king by the priest Jehoiada (2 Kings 11).
He collected money and repaired the house of the LORD (2 Kings 12).
After Jehoiada died, he served idols and had Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned (2 Chronicles 24).
His own servants conspired against him and killed him (2 Chronicles 24).

joram_804.name: Joram
joram_804.who: King of Israel, son of Ahab and Jezebel, who was killed by Jehu.
key: He became king of Israel after his brother Ahaziah died without a son (2 Kings 1).
With Jehoshaphat he fought Moab, and Elisha foretold God's supply of water (2 Kings 3).
Wounded by the Syrians, he returned to Jezreel to recover (2 Kings 8).
Jehu shot him with an arrow, and his body was thrown on Naboth's land (2 Kings 9).

ben-hadad_452.name: Ben-hadad
ben-hadad_452.who: King of Syria in Damascus, son of Tabrimmon, who attacked Israel at the request of King Asa.
key: Asa of Judah sent him silver and gold to break his treaty with Baasha (1 Kings 15).
He attacked Israelite cities including Ijon, Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah (1 Kings 15).
The seer Hanani rebuked Asa for relying on him rather than the LORD (2 Chronicles 16).
A Syrian king named Ben-hadad besieged Samaria in Ahab's day and was defeated (1 Kings 20).
Jeremiah foretold fire devouring the strongholds of Ben-hadad in Damascus (Jeremiah 49).

hadarezer_1340.name: Hadadezer
hadarezer_1340.who: Son of Rehob and king of Zobah in Syria, defeated in battle by David.
key: David defeated him as he went to restore his power at the Euphrates (2 Samuel 8).
David took the gold shields of his servants to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8).
He sent Syrian forces from beyond the Euphrates against Israel, but they were defeated (2 Samuel 10).
His vassal kings made peace with Israel and served them (2 Samuel 10).
Rezon, who later troubled Solomon, had fled from him (1 Kings 11).

ishmael_630.name: Ishmael
ishmael_630.who: Son of Abraham by Hagar the Egyptian, and father of twelve tribal princes.
key: The angel of the LORD told Hagar to name her son Ishmael (Genesis 16).
He was circumcised at thirteen, and God promised to make him a great nation (Genesis 17).
He and Hagar were sent away, and God provided water in the wilderness (Genesis 21).
He and Isaac buried Abraham, and he died at 137 years old (Genesis 25).
Esau married his daughter to please his father Isaac (Genesis 28).

james_717.name: James
james_717.who: Apostle of Jesus, son of Zebedee and brother of John, who was martyred by Herod.
key: Jesus called him and John from mending nets with their father (Matthew 4).
He was appointed one of the Twelve, and Jesus called the brothers Boanerges (Mark 3).
He witnessed Jesus' transfiguration with Peter and John (Matthew 17).
He and John asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in glory (Mark 10).
Herod Agrippa had him killed with the sword (Acts 12).

meshach_2092.name: Meshach
meshach_2092.who: One of Daniel's three Judean friends in Babylon, kept safe by God in the fiery furnace.
key: Taken to Babylon, he was renamed Meshach and avoided the king's food (Daniel 1).
He prayed with Daniel for God to reveal the king's dream (Daniel 2).
Nebuchadnezzar appointed him over the affairs of the province of Babylon (Daniel 2).
He refused to worship the golden image and was thrown into the furnace (Daniel 3).
He came out unharmed, and the king praised their God (Daniel 3).

micaiah_2054.name: Micaiah
micaiah_2054.who: Prophet of the LORD, son of Imlah, who foretold King Ahab's defeat and death in battle.
key: Ahab hated him because he never prophesied good concerning him (1 Kings 22).
He saw Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd (1 Kings 22).
He described a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab's prophets (1 Kings 22).
Zedekiah struck him, and Ahab had him imprisoned on bread and water (1 Kings 22).
The same account is recorded in the history of Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 18).

nabal_2126.name: Nabal
nabal_2126.who: Wealthy but harsh Calebite of Maon, the first husband of Abigail.
key: He insulted David's men and refused them provisions at sheep-shearing time (1 Samuel 25).
His wife Abigail brought food to David without telling him (1 Samuel 25).
Hearing what happened, his heart failed, and the LORD struck him ten days later (1 Samuel 25).
Abigail, the widow of Nabal, went with David to Hebron (2 Samuel 2).

naboth_2127.name: Naboth
naboth_2127.who: Man of Jezreel who was killed through Jezebel's plot after refusing to sell his vineyard to Ahab.
key: He refused to give King Ahab his family inheritance (1 Kings 21).
Jezebel arranged false witnesses, and he was stoned to death (1 Kings 21).
Elijah announced the LORD's judgment on Ahab for taking his vineyard (1 Kings 21).
Jehu had King Joram's body thrown onto Naboth's plot of ground (2 Kings 9).

shadrach_1398.name: Shadrach
shadrach_1398.who: One of Daniel's three Judean friends in Babylon, kept safe by God in the fiery furnace.
key: Taken to Babylon, he was renamed Shadrach and avoided the king's food (Daniel 1).
He prayed with Daniel for God to reveal the king's dream (Daniel 2).
Nebuchadnezzar appointed him over the affairs of the province of Babylon (Daniel 2).
He refused to worship the golden image and was thrown into the furnace (Daniel 3).
He came out unharmed, and the king praised their God (Daniel 3).

ahithophel_162.name: Ahithophel
ahithophel_162.who: David's trusted counselor from Giloh who joined Absalom's rebellion.
key: He joined Absalom's conspiracy, and David prayed his counsel would become foolishness (2 Samuel 15).
He advised Absalom to go in to his father's concubines publicly (2 Samuel 16).
His counsel was esteemed as if one consulted the word of God (2 Samuel 16).
When Hushai's advice was followed instead, he went home and hanged himself (2 Samuel 17).
He is listed as the king's counselor in David's administration (1 Chronicles 27).

machir_1877.name: Machir
machir_1877.who: Son of Manasseh and grandson of Joseph, ancestor of the Machirite clan and father of Gilead.
key: His children were born on Joseph's knees (Genesis 50).
He was the father of Gilead and head of the Machirite clan (Numbers 26).
His descendants took Gilead, and Moses gave it to them (Numbers 32).
Hezron married his daughter, who bore him Segub (1 Chronicles 2).

micah_2049.name: Micah
micah_2049.who: Man of the hill country of Ephraim who set up a household shrine with idols in the time of the judges.
key: He returned stolen silver to his mother, who had an idol made from it (Judges 17).
He made a shrine with an ephod and household gods and installed his son as priest (Judges 17).
He hired a wandering Levite to serve as his priest (Judges 17).
The Danites took his idols and his priest, and he could not stop them (Judges 18).

ornan_289.name: Ornan
ornan_289.who: Jebusite whose threshing floor in Jerusalem David bought, later the site of Solomon's temple.
key: The angel bringing plague stopped beside his threshing floor (2 Samuel 24).
He saw the angel while threshing wheat and hid with his sons (1 Chronicles 21).
He offered David the floor freely, but David insisted on paying full price (1 Chronicles 21).
Solomon built the temple on his threshing floor on Mount Moriah (2 Chronicles 3).

shem_2613.name: Shem
shem_2613.who: Son of Noah who survived the flood and became ancestor of Abraham and the Israelites.
key: He entered the ark with Noah and his family (Genesis 7).
He and Japheth covered their father's nakedness and were blessed by Noah (Genesis 9).
His descendants are listed in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
He fathered Arpachshad two years after the flood and lived 600 years (Genesis 11).
He is named in the genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).

silas_2740.name: Silas
silas_2740.who: Leader in the Jerusalem church who became Paul's missionary companion.
key: He was chosen to carry the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch, then joined Paul (Acts 15).
He and Paul were beaten and jailed in Philippi, then freed by an earthquake (Acts 16).
He preached with Paul in Thessalonica and Berea (Acts 17).
He is named with Paul and Timothy in greeting the Thessalonians (1 Thessalonians 1).
Peter wrote his first letter with the help of Silvanus (1 Peter 5).

sisera_2757.name: Sisera
sisera_2757.who: Commander of King Jabin's Canaanite army, defeated by Barak and killed by Jael.
key: With 900 iron chariots he oppressed Israel for twenty years (Judges 4).
The LORD routed his army before Barak, and he fled on foot (Judges 4).
Jael killed him with a tent peg while he slept in her tent (Judges 4).
Deborah's song describes his death and his mother waiting at the window (Judges 5).
Samuel recalled that God sold Israel into his hand when they forgot the LORD (1 Samuel 12).

cain_533.name: Cain
cain_533.who: Firstborn son of Adam and Eve, who murdered his brother Abel.
key: A farmer, he brought an offering the LORD did not regard with favor (Genesis 4).
He killed his brother Abel in the field (Genesis 4).
The LORD cursed him to be a wanderer but put a mark on him for protection (Genesis 4).
He built a city and named it after his son Enoch (Genesis 4).
John says he was of the evil one and murdered his brother (1 John 3).

darius_978.name: Darius
darius_978.who: King of Persia during whose reign the second temple in Jerusalem was rebuilt and completed.
key: Work on the temple stopped until the second year of his reign (Ezra 4).
Haggai prophesied in his second year, urging the people to rebuild (Haggai 1).
The governor Tattenai wrote to him questioning the temple's rebuilding (Ezra 5).
He found Cyrus's decree and ordered the work supported from royal revenue (Ezra 6).
The temple was finished in the sixth year of his reign (Ezra 6).

jehoram_803.name: Jehoram
jehoram_803.who: King of Judah, son of Jehoshaphat, who married Ahab's daughter and followed the ways of Israel's kings.
key: When he became king, he killed all his brothers with the sword (2 Chronicles 21).
He walked in the way of Ahab's house, for Ahab's daughter was his wife (2 Kings 8).
Edom and Libnah revolted from Judah's rule during his reign (2 Kings 8).
A letter from Elijah warned him of judgment for his sins (2 Chronicles 21).
He died of a painful bowel disease, and no one regretted his death (2 Chronicles 21).

jethro_2431.name: Jethro
jethro_2431.who: Priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, who gave Moses wise counsel in the wilderness.
key: Moses helped his daughters at a well and later married his daughter Zipporah (Exodus 2).
Moses was keeping his flock when God spoke from the burning bush (Exodus 3).
Moses asked his permission to return to Egypt (Exodus 4).
He rejoiced at the LORD's deliverance of Israel and offered sacrifices to God (Exodus 18).
He advised Moses to appoint capable men to judge the people (Exodus 18).

michal_2073.name: Michal
michal_2073.who: Younger daughter of King Saul and the first wife of David.
key: She loved David, and Saul gave her to him as wife (1 Samuel 18).
She helped David escape through a window and deceived Saul's messengers (1 Samuel 19).
Saul gave her to Palti son of Laish while David was a fugitive (1 Samuel 25).
David demanded her return, and her husband followed her weeping (2 Samuel 3).
She despised David for dancing before the ark and had no child (2 Samuel 6).

nethaniah_2198.name: Nethaniah
nethaniah_2198.who: Son of Elishama of the royal family, known as the father of Ishmael who assassinated Gedaliah.
key: His son Ishmael killed Gedaliah, the governor appointed by Babylon (2 Kings 25).
Johanan warned Gedaliah that Ishmael son of Nethaniah planned to kill him (Jeremiah 40).
Ishmael son of Nethaniah murdered Gedaliah and others at Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).

philip_2347.name: Philip
philip_2347.who: One of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church, later known as Philip the evangelist.
key: He was chosen as one of the seven to oversee the daily distribution (Acts 6).
He proclaimed Christ in Samaria, and many believed and were baptized (Acts 8).
He explained Isaiah to an Ethiopian official and baptized him (Acts 8).
He hosted Paul in Caesarea, where his four unmarried daughters prophesied (Acts 21).

phinehas_2349.name: Phinehas
phinehas_2349.who: Priest, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, known for his zeal for the LORD.
key: He killed Zimri and Cozbi, stopping the plague, and received a covenant of perpetual priesthood (Numbers 25).
He went with Israel's army against Midian, carrying the holy vessels and trumpets (Numbers 31).
He led the delegation questioning the altar built by the eastern tribes (Joshua 22).
He inquired of the LORD at Bethel during the war with Benjamin (Judges 20).
The psalmist says his deed was counted to him as righteousness (Psalms 106).

rabshakeh_2384.name: Rabshakeh
rabshakeh_2384.who: High-ranking Assyrian official sent by Sennacherib to demand Jerusalem's surrender.
key: Sennacherib sent him with a great army to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem (2 Kings 18).
He mocked Judah's trust in the LORD and in Egypt (2 Kings 18).
He refused to speak Aramaic and shouted to the people in Hebrew (2 Kings 18).
He returned to find the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah (2 Kings 19).
Isaiah records the same confrontation at Jerusalem (Isaiah 36).

amon_236.name: Amon
amon_236.who: King of Judah, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, who did evil and was assassinated.
key: He became king at twenty-two and reigned two years, doing evil like Manasseh (2 Kings 21).
He did not humble himself before the LORD as his father had (2 Chronicles 33).
His servants conspired and killed him in his house (2 Kings 21).
The people killed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king (2 Kings 21).
He is listed in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

athaliah_359.name: Athaliah
athaliah_359.who: Daughter of Ahab who seized the throne of Judah and ruled six years.
key: She was the wife of King Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8).
She counseled her son King Ahaziah to act wickedly (2 Chronicles 22).
After Ahaziah died, she destroyed the royal family and ruled the land (2 Kings 11).
The priest Jehoiada crowned young Joash, and she was put to death (2 Kings 11).
Her sons had broken into the temple and used its holy things for the Baals (2 Chronicles 24).

james_719.name: James
james_719.who: Brother of Jesus who became a leader of the Jerusalem church and wrote the letter of James.
key: He is named among Jesus' brothers by the people of Nazareth (Matthew 13).
Peter sent word to him after being freed from prison (Acts 12).
He spoke at the Jerusalem council and proposed its decision (Acts 15).
The risen Jesus appeared to him (1 Corinthians 15).
Paul calls him a pillar of the Jerusalem church (Galatians 2).

jephunneh_840.name: Jephunneh
jephunneh_840.who: Kenizzite of the tribe of Judah, known as the father of Caleb, one of the two faithful spies.
key: His son Caleb represented Judah among the twelve spies sent into Canaan (Numbers 13).
The LORD promised that Caleb son of Jephunneh would enter the land (Numbers 14).
Caleb is called the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite (Numbers 32).
Joshua gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance (Joshua 14).

johanan_1666.name: Johanan
johanan_1666.who: Son of Kareah and a Judean army captain who led the remnant to Egypt after Jerusalem fell.
key: He warned Governor Gedaliah that Ishmael planned to kill him (Jeremiah 40).
He rescued the captives Ishmael had taken from Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).
He asked Jeremiah to seek the LORD's guidance and promised to obey (Jeremiah 42).
He rejected the LORD's word and took the remnant, including Jeremiah, to Egypt (Jeremiah 43).

joseph_1715.name: Joseph
joseph_1715.who: Carpenter of Nazareth from David's line, husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus.
key: An angel told him in a dream to take Mary as his wife (Matthew 1).
He went to Bethlehem for the census, where Jesus was born (Luke 2).
Warned in a dream, he fled with Mary and Jesus to Egypt (Matthew 2).
He returned and settled the family in Nazareth (Matthew 2).
He and Mary found twelve-year-old Jesus in the temple (Luke 2).

nebuzar-adan_2169.name: Nebuzaradan
nebuzar-adan_2169.who: Captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard who burned Jerusalem and carried its people into exile.
key: He burned the temple, the king's house, and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25).
He carried the people into exile, leaving some of the poorest behind (2 Kings 25).
He freed Jeremiah from chains and let him stay with Gedaliah (Jeremiah 40).
He took 745 more Judeans into exile in Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year (Jeremiah 52).

pharez_2338.name: Perez
pharez_2338.who: Son of Judah and Tamar, twin of Zerah, and ancestor of King David and Jesus.
key: He was born a twin, breaking out ahead of his brother Zerah (Genesis 38).
He went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
He was the head of the clan of the Perezites (Numbers 26).
The elders blessed Boaz's house to be like the house of Perez (Ruth 4).
He is listed in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

philip_2344.name: Philip
philip_2344.who: One of the twelve apostles, from Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus.
key: Jesus called him to follow, and he brought Nathanael to Jesus (John 1).
He is listed among the twelve apostles (Matthew 10).
Jesus tested him by asking where to buy bread for the crowd (John 6).
Some Greeks came to him asking to see Jesus (John 12).
He asked Jesus to show them the Father (John 14).

shechem_2588.name: Shechem
shechem_2588.who: Hivite prince, son of Hamor, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
key: Jacob bought land near the city from the sons of Hamor (Genesis 33).
He seized and violated Dinah, then asked to marry her (Genesis 34).
He agreed that his city's men would be circumcised (Genesis 34).
Simeon and Levi killed him, his father, and the men of the city (Genesis 34).
Joseph's bones were buried on land bought from the sons of Hamor (Joshua 24).

shimei_2684.name: Shimei
shimei_2684.who: Benjaminite of Saul's clan, son of Gera, who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: He cursed David and threw stones as David fled Jerusalem (2 Samuel 16).
David refused to let Abishai kill him (2 Samuel 16).
He begged forgiveness when David returned, and David spared him (2 Samuel 19).
David charged Solomon not to leave him unpunished (1 Kings 2).
He broke his oath to stay in Jerusalem and was executed (1 Kings 2).

abigail_26.name: Abigail
abigail_26.who: Wise and discerning wife of Nabal who later became a wife of David.
key: She brought provisions to David and kept him from taking vengeance (1 Samuel 25).
After Nabal died, David sent for her and she became his wife (1 Samuel 25).
She lived with David among the Philistines at Gath (1 Samuel 27).
Amalekites captured her at Ziklag, and David rescued her (1 Samuel 30).
She bore David's second son at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).

asahel_320.name: Asahel
asahel_320.who: Swift-footed nephew of David and brother of Joab, killed by Abner in battle.
key: Fast as a wild gazelle, he chased Abner after the battle at Gibeon (2 Samuel 2).
Abner warned him repeatedly, then killed him with the butt of his spear (2 Samuel 2).
Joab killed Abner at Hebron to avenge Asahel's death (2 Samuel 3).
He is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
He commanded the fourth month's division, followed by his son Zebadiah (1 Chronicles 27).

ham_1359.name: Ham
ham_1359.who: Son of Noah who survived the flood and became ancestor of Egypt, Cush, Put, and Canaan.
key: He entered the ark with Noah and his family (Genesis 7).
He saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers, and Noah cursed Canaan (Genesis 9).
His descendants, including Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan, are listed (Genesis 10).
The psalmist calls Egypt the land of Ham (Psalms 105).

jehoahaz_784.name: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz_784.who: King of Israel, son of Jehu, who reigned seventeen years in Samaria.
key: He succeeded his father Jehu as king of Israel (2 Kings 10).
He did evil, so the LORD gave Israel into the hand of Hazael of Syria (2 Kings 13).
He sought the LORD, who gave Israel a savior (2 Kings 13).
His army was reduced to fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand soldiers (2 Kings 13).
His son Joash reigned in his place (2 Kings 13).

jeroboam_873.name: Jeroboam
jeroboam_873.who: King of Israel, son of Joash, who restored Israel's borders; often called Jeroboam II.
key: He reigned forty-one years in Samaria and did evil in the LORD's sight (2 Kings 14).
He restored Israel's border as the LORD spoke through Jonah (2 Kings 14).
Hosea prophesied during his reign (Hosea 1).
Amos prophesied in his days, and Amaziah the priest reported Amos to him (Amos 7).
His son Zechariah succeeded him and reigned six months (2 Kings 15).

kareah_919.name: Kareah
kareah_919.who: Father of Johanan and Jonathan, army captains in Judah after the fall of Jerusalem.
key: His son Johanan came to Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25).
Johanan and Jonathan, his sons, joined Gedaliah with their men (Jeremiah 40).
Johanan son of Kareah rescued captives from Ishmael (Jeremiah 41).
Johanan son of Kareah led the remnant to Egypt against the LORD's word (Jeremiah 43).

manoah_1933.name: Manoah
manoah_1933.who: Danite from Zorah and father of Samson.
key: The angel of the LORD told his barren wife she would bear a son (Judges 13).
He prayed that the man of God would return to teach them (Judges 13).
The angel ascended in the flame of his offering (Judges 13).
His parents went with Samson to Timnah about a Philistine wife (Judges 14).
Samson was buried in Manoah's tomb between Zorah and Eshtaol (Judges 16).

mary_1943.name: Mary Magdalene
mary_1943.who: Follower of Jesus, freed from seven demons, who first saw the risen Lord.
key: Jesus cast seven demons from her, and she supported his ministry (Luke 8).
She stood near the cross with Jesus' mother (John 19).
She watched where Jesus' body was laid in the tomb (Mark 15).
She came early to the tomb and found it empty (Mark 16).
The risen Jesus appeared to her, and she told the disciples (John 20).

mephibosheth_1999.name: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth_1999.who: Son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul, lame in both feet, shown kindness by David.
key: He became lame at five when his nurse fell while fleeing (2 Samuel 4).
David restored Saul's land to him and he ate at the king's table (2 Samuel 9).
Ziba claimed he stayed in Jerusalem hoping to regain the kingdom (2 Samuel 16).
He met David returning, having not cared for his feet or beard (2 Samuel 19).
David spared him because of his oath to Jonathan (2 Samuel 21).

ner_2181.name: Ner
ner_2181.who: Benjaminite, son of Abiel, uncle of Saul, and father of Saul's army commander Abner.
key: His son Abner was commander of Saul's army (1 Samuel 14).
Abner son of Ner lay beside Saul when David entered the camp (1 Samuel 26).
Abner son of Ner made Ish-bosheth king over Israel (2 Samuel 2).
Joab killed Abner son of Ner at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
He appears in the family line of Saul (1 Chronicles 9).

sennacherib_2489.name: Sennacherib
sennacherib_2489.who: King of Assyria who invaded Judah and besieged Jerusalem during Hezekiah's reign.
key: He captured Judah's fortified cities, and Hezekiah paid him tribute (2 Kings 18).
He sent the Rabshakeh to demand Jerusalem's surrender (2 Kings 18).
Hezekiah spread his threatening letter before the LORD and prayed (2 Kings 19).
The angel of the LORD struck 185,000 in his camp (2 Kings 19).
His sons killed him while he worshiped in the house of Nisroch (2 Kings 19).
